proposedTopics.title: Public-key cryptography & wallets
proposedTopics.description: An EOA is controlled by a keypair, while a wallet is the interface that manages signing authority: the private key signs, and the public key derives the 20-byte address (keccak of the pubkey, last 20 bytes). Losing an unbacked-up key means losing control; there is no protocol reset.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: run `cast wallet new` in web3-practice; in contracts/phase01/README.md explain, in your own words, how the address is derived from the public key and why the private key must never touch the chain. Done when: you can state the derivation (pubkey → keccak256 → last 20 bytes) without looking.

proposedTopics.title: SEC1 public-key serialization & address derivation
proposedTopics.description: A secp256k1 public key is a curve point (x,y), not an ECDSA operation. SEC1 encodes it as 33-byte compressed 02/03||x or 65-byte uncompressed 04||x||y; Ethereum derives an address from Keccak-256 of the raw 64-byte x||y, excluding 04, then keeps the final 20 bytes. Confusing bits with hex characters, SHA3-256 with Keccak-256, or hashing the SEC1 prefix produces the wrong address.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: in scripts/phase01/address-derivation.ts, use a fixed non-secret 32-byte scalar and an established secp256k1 primitive to emit compressed and uncompressed SEC1 keys, validate their 33/65-byte prefixes and lengths, strip 04, Keccak-hash x||y, and slice the final 20 bytes; compare with `cast wallet address --private-key`. Reject 0 and scalars >= curve order, and assert that SHA3-256 or hashing 04||x||y disagrees. Done when: one command runs deterministic assertions for the expected address, representations, invalid-scalar boundaries, and both deliberate wrong-hash cases.

proposedTopics.title: ECDSA signing, verification & recovery
proposedTopics.description: ECDSA signs a message digest with a private scalar and lets verifiers check authorization with the public point; Ethereum also carries recovery parity so the signer can be recovered. A valid signature proves authorization of exact bytes, not safety or intent. Nonce reuse, high-s malleability, missing domain separation, ambiguous message prefixes, and accepting a recovered zero address are practical failure modes.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: in scripts/phase01/sign-recover.ts, hash a fixed message with and without the EIP-191 prefix, sign locally, split r/s/recovery parity, recover the address, and verify it equals the address-derivation lab; mutate one message byte and assert failure. Add assertions for low-s normalization and domain separation, and never print a real secret. Done when: deterministic checks prove exact-byte authorization, recovery, mutation failure, prefix mismatch, and the low-s boundary.

proposedTopics.description: A type-2 transaction carries chainId, nonce, maxPriorityFeePerGas, maxFeePerGas, gasLimit, to, value, data, accessList, and a signature (yParity, r, s); legacy transactions use v, r, s. The nonce enforces sender ordering and replay protection; `data` is the ABI-encoded call.

proposedTopics.title: RLP & typed transaction serialization
proposedTopics.description: RLP encodes byte strings and nested lists with length prefixes; integers are minimally encoded big-endian byte strings, so zero is the empty byte string rather than byte 00. EIP-2718 typed transactions prepend a type byte to an opaque payload, and a type-2 signing hash covers 0x02||rlp(unsigned fields) while the broadcast form appends yParity, r, and s. One wrong field order, integer encoding, or signed/unsigned boundary changes the hash and signer.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: in scripts/phase01/type2-transaction.ts, implement the small RLP subset needed for one fixed EIP-1559 transaction using only byte/string primitives; encode its unsigned signing payload, Keccak-hash it, sign it, append yParity/r/s, and recover the sender. Compare every hex result with `cast mktx --offline` or a maintained client library. Done when: deterministic assertions cover single-byte, short-string, long-length, zero-integer, nested-list, type-byte, field-order, signing-hash, raw-transaction, and recovered-sender cases.

proposedTopics.title: Stack / memory / storage / calldata
proposedTopics.description: The EVM's working areas differ in lifetime, mutability, addressing, and cost: the stack is a 1024-word operand workspace, memory is byte-addressed and expansion-priced, storage is persistent 32-byte-slot state, and calldata is immutable call input that can avoid memory copies. Choosing the wrong location is a root of both bugs and gas waste.

proposedTopics.title: What a blockchain is
proposedTopics.description: A blockchain is an append-only ledger of blocks, each committing to its parent by hash, replicated across many nodes that agree on one history via consensus. Tampering with an old block changes its hash and breaks every child, so the chain is immutable in practice. Trust comes from cryptography and replication, not an operator.

proposedTopics.title: Hashing & Merkle trees
proposedTopics.description: keccak256 is Ethereum's workhorse hash: deterministic, one-way, collision-resistant, fixed 32-byte output. Merkle trees hash data in pairs up to a single root, so one 32-byte root commits to a whole set and any member is provable with a log-sized branch. Block headers and state use this to make tampering detectable.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: in scripts/phase01/merkle.ts, hash four fixed leaves with Ethereum Keccak-256, define and document pair ordering, compute the root, generate a proof for every leaf, and implement verification; compare one hash with `cast keccak`. Add negative checks for a mutated leaf, wrong sibling order, odd leaf count policy, SHA3-256 substitution, and ambiguous packed concatenation. Done when: deterministic assertions verify every membership proof, reject every mutation, and show proof length grows as ceil(log2(n)) under the documented duplication rule.

proposedTopics.title: Mnemonics & HD wallets
proposedTopics.description: A BIP-39 mnemonic encodes entropy plus a checksum and is converted into a seed; BIP-32 derives a tree of keypairs from it, BIP-44 defines the path hierarchy, and SLIP-44 assigns coin type 60 to Ethereum (e.g. m/44'/60'/0'/0/0). One phrase therefore backs up an unlimited set of addresses, and anyone holding it controls every derived key.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: run `cast wallet new-mnemonic` then derive two addresses with `cast wallet derive-private-key`; in contracts/phase01/hd-wallets.md record the path and both addresses. Done when: you can explain how changing the last path index yields a fresh address from the same seed.

proposedTopics.title: Mnemonic-to-seed & child-key derivation
proposedTopics.description: BIP-39 maps entropy plus checksum bits to word indices, then uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 with NFKD-normalized mnemonic and salt `mnemonic` plus passphrase to produce a 64-byte seed. BIP-32 uses HMAC-SHA512 chain codes and scalar arithmetic for child keys; hardened derivation includes the private key and cannot be reproduced from an extended public key. A passphrase creates a valid but different wallet, and path, normalization, endian, or hardened-index mistakes silently produce different accounts.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: in scripts/phase01/hd-derivation.ts, reproduce one official BIP-39 vector from entropy through checksum/word indices and PBKDF2 seed, then derive Ethereum paths m/44'/60'/0'/0/0 and /1 with a maintained BIP-32 primitive. Assert the seed and both addresses against vectors and `cast wallet derive-private-key`; add a passphrase and show that it deterministically changes the root. Done when: tests catch a bad checksum, wrong NFKD/salt, wrong endian index, omitted hardened bit, and changed final address index.

proposedTopics.title: Raw Ethereum JSON-RPC
proposedTopics.description: Ethereum JSON-RPC is a transport-neutral request/response boundary: a client sends jsonrpc 2.0, an id, method, and positional parameters, then receives exactly one result or error. Quantities use minimal 0x-prefixed hex while byte data preserves even-length bytes; block tags change the state snapshot being queried. HTTP success does not imply RPC success, eth_call simulates without committing, and eth_sendRawTransaction accepts already-signed bytes rather than custody of a private key.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: in scripts/phase01/raw-rpc.ts, use Node's built-in fetch to call a local Anvil node directly—no viem/ethers wrapper—for eth_chainId, eth_getBalance, eth_getBlockByNumber, eth_call, and a deliberately invalid method. Validate id correlation and result-versus-error, parse hex quantities as bigint, keep DATA as bytes, and abort on timeout. Done when: one command starts from a configurable RPC URL and assertions cover success, RPC error under HTTP 200, malformed response, timeout, latest versus fixed block tags, and no floating-point balance conversion.

proposedTopics.title: EOAs vs contract accounts
proposedTopics.description: Ethereum has two account types sharing one 20-byte address space: EOAs, controlled by signing authority, and contract accounts, controlled by code with no private key. proposedTopics.title: Nonce & replay protection
proposedTopics.description: An EOA has a monotonically increasing account nonce used as a sequence counter. A normal sender transaction is valid only at the account's exact next nonce, which forces ordering and blocks replay after inclusion. EIP-155 folds chainId into legacy transaction signatures so a mainnet transaction cannot be replayed unchanged on another chain.

proposedTopics.title: The EVM as a state machine
proposedTopics.description: The EVM is a deterministic state machine: a transaction maps the pre-state (world state = mapping of address → account state, each with balance/nonce/code/storage) to a post-state, gas-metered every step. All nodes re-running the same transaction with the same state and block context reach the same result.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: in scripts/phase01/evm-trace.ts, implement a deliberately tiny interpreter for PUSH1, ADD, MSTORE, MLOAD, SSTORE, SLOAD, STOP, and REVERT with program counter, 256-bit wrapping stack values, memory, persistent storage, and a gas counter. Execute fixed bytecode step by step and emit a trace; assert identical input yields identical post-state and REVERT discards state writes. Done when: tests catch stack underflow, invalid opcode, out-of-gas, 2^256 overflow, memory expansion, and reverted storage while a successful run matches `cast run --trace` or evm.codes.

proposedTopics.title: Opcodes & the interpreter loop
proposedTopics.description: EVM bytecode is a sequence of 1-byte opcodes run in a fetch-decode-execute loop over a program counter, a 1024-slot stack, and gas. Each opcode (ADD, SLOAD, CALL, …) has a specified stack effect and gas rule, with many costs depending on memory growth or execution context; the loop halts on STOP/RETURN/REVERT or exceptional failure. evm.codes is the interactive playground used in the Build.

proposedTopics.title: World state & Merkle Patricia tries
proposedTopics.description: Ethereum's world state lives in a Merkle Patricia Trie keyed by account address; each account's storage is itself a trie. proposedPrompts.promptText: How is an Ethereum address derived from a private key, and what is irreversible about it?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: privkey → (secp256k1) pubkey → keccak256(pubkey) → last 20 bytes = address. One-way at each step; a lost private key is unrecoverable and there is no admin reset.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Name the fields of an EIP-1559 type-2 transaction and say how replay is prevented.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: chainId, nonce, maxPriorityFeePerGas, maxFeePerGas, gasLimit, to, value, data, accessList, yParity, r, s. The sender nonce blocks same-chain replay after inclusion; chainId domain-separates the signature across chains.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Break down what a sender pays per gas under EIP-1559, and where each part goes.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: base fee (burned, set by protocol from block fullness) + effective tip (to the proposer), where effectiveTip = min(maxPriorityFeePerGas, maxFeePerGas - baseFee). Total = gasUsed × (baseFee + effectiveTip).

proposedPrompts.promptText: Compare stack, memory, storage, and calldata by lifetime, mutability, and gas cost drivers.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Stack is 256-bit operand workspace with top-16 access; memory is mutable per-call scratch with expansion cost; storage is persistent state with context-dependent SLOAD/SSTORE costs; calldata is immutable call input and avoids a memory copy for read-only external arguments.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Why is a blockchain immutable in practice, rather than by decree?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Each block commits to its parent, so altering an old block changes descendant commitments; replacing that history must overcome honest fork choice, finality, and economic security. Pitfall: immutability is economic and consensus-backed, not absolute.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What does a Merkle root let you prove, and how large is the proof?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: A single 32-byte root commits to an entire set; membership of any leaf is provable with a branch of ~log2(n) sibling hashes, without revealing the rest. Pitfall: it proves inclusion, not exclusion (that needs a sorted/sparse variant).

proposedPrompts.promptText: Why can one seed phrase back up an unlimited number of Ethereum addresses?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: BIP-32 hierarchical-deterministic derivation expands the BIP-39 seed into a tree of child keys along a BIP-44 path (m/44'/60'/…); each index is a new keypair. Pitfall: the phrase is the master secret — leaking it compromises every derived account.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What is JSON-RPC's role, and why does Ethereum want many independent clients?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: JSON-RPC is the request/response API (eth_call, eth_sendRawTransaction, …) apps use to read and write chain state. Client diversity means one client's bug can't halt or split the network. Pitfall: a public RPC is trusted infrastructure — it can lie unless you verify.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How do EOAs and contract accounts differ in control and fields?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: EOA authority signs transaction authorizations; contract-account behavior is code-controlled and only runs when called. Both have nonce, balance, codeHash, and storageRoot fields. EIP-7702 lets an EOA delegate code without giving a contract account a private signing key.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How does the nonce prevent replay and enforce ordering?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Each EOA tx must use its exact next sequential nonce, so a mined tx (nonce consumed) can't re-execute and txs process in order. EIP-155 adds chainId to the signature to block cross-chain replay. Pitfall: a missing lower nonce stalls all higher-nonce txs.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Name the modern Ethereum transaction types and what makes each distinct.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Legacy wire transactions are untyped RLP (often reported by RPC as type 0x0); typed envelopes are 0x1 access-list (2930), 0x2 dynamic-fee (1559, the default), 0x3 blob (4844), and 0x4 set-code (7702). Pitfall: blob data isn't in calldata — it rides in a separate, short-lived sidecar.

proposedPrompts.topicTitle: The EVM as a state machine
proposedPrompts.promptText: In what sense is the EVM a state machine?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Each transaction deterministically maps world state plus explicit transaction/block context to a new world state, metered by gas. Nodes agree because there is no live wall-clock input, nondeterministic RNG, or external I/O during execution.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Describe the EVM's interpreter loop and its working memory.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Fetch opcode at PC → decode → execute against the 1024-deep stack (plus memory/storage), charge gas, advance or jump PC; halt on STOP/RETURN/REVERT or out-of-gas. Pitfall: stack overflow (>1024) or underflow reverts the whole call.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Where does the value of `mapping(k=>v) m` declared at slot p live in storage?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: At keccak256(abi.encode(k, p)); the mapping itself occupies slot p only as a placeholder. Dynamic arrays keep length at p and data at keccak256(p). Pitfall: `private` hides nothing — any slot is publicly readable.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What does the block header's stateRoot commit to, and why does it matter?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: stateRoot commits to the account trie. An account proof authenticates the account and its storageRoot against stateRoot; a separate storage proof authenticates the slot against that storageRoot along the slot key's hashed-nibble path. Changing a slot changes the storage root and ultimately stateRoot.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Compare compressed and uncompressed SEC1 public keys and identify the exact bytes Ethereum hashes for an address.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Compressed is 33 bytes: 02/03 plus x, with the prefix encoding y parity. Uncompressed is 65 bytes: 04||x||y. Ethereum hashes the raw 64-byte x||y without 04 using Keccak-256, then takes the final 20 bytes. Pitfalls: 256 bits = 64 hex characters, and SHA3-256 is not Ethereum Keccak-256.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the byte pipeline that derives and validates an Ethereum address from a 32-byte private scalar.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Reject scalar 0 or >= secp256k1 order; derive point (x,y) with an audited curve primitive; serialize 04||x||y; hash x||y with Keccak-256; slice bytes 12..31; compare against a client/cast vector. Include wrong-prefix and SHA3 negative assertions.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What does a valid Ethereum signature prove, and which practical boundaries can still fail?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: It proves control of the signing scalar authorized the exact digest. It does not prove safety or human intent. Boundaries include nonce reuse, wrong message prefix/domain, high-s malleability, parity/recovery mistakes, and accepting a zero recovered address.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Implement a deterministic sign-and-recover check for a fixed EIP-191 message.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Construct the EIP-191-prefixed digest, sign locally, enforce low-s, carry recovery parity, recover the public key/address, and assert it equals the independently derived address. Mutating one byte or omitting the prefix must not recover the expected signer.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Trace a BIP-39 mnemonic into Ethereum child key m/44'/60'/0'/0/0 and name the silent divergence hazards.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Entropy+checksum bits map to 11-bit word indices; NFKD mnemonic enters PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 with salt `mnemonic`+NFKD passphrase to make a 64-byte seed; BIP-32 HMAC chain codes derive hardened and normal children; BIP-44 path selects Ethereum. Wrong normalization, endian index, hardened bit, passphrase, or path yields a valid different wallet.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write deterministic checks for one BIP-39 vector and the first two Ethereum BIP-44 addresses.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Assert entropy checksum and word indices, PBKDF2 seed, root/child derivation, m/44'/60'/0'/0/0 and /1 addresses, checksum rejection, passphrase divergence, and hardened-index encoding against official vectors and cast.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What bytes are signed and broadcast for an EIP-1559 type-2 transaction?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signing digest = keccak256(0x02 || rlp([chainId, nonce, maxPriorityFeePerGas, maxFeePerGas, gasLimit, to, value, data, accessList])). Broadcast bytes append yParity, r, s inside the RLP list. Integers are minimal big-endian bytes; zero is the empty byte string.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Implement the RLP subset and type-2 signing pipeline for one fixed transaction vector.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Cover single bytes <0x80, short/long strings and lists, minimal integer encoding, nested access lists, leading type byte, unsigned field order, signing digest, appended signature, and recovered sender; compare complete hex with cast or a maintained client.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Separate the HTTP, JSON-RPC, and Ethereum-encoding boundaries in a raw node request.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: HTTP 200 can still contain a JSON-RPC error. Match response id; require exactly result or error. QUANTITY is minimal hex parsed as bigint; DATA is even-length bytes. A block tag selects state. eth_call simulates; eth_sendRawTransaction submits signed bytes.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a dependency-free Node JSON-RPC caller that safely returns an Ethereum quantity.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: POST jsonrpc/id/method/params with built-in fetch and AbortSignal timeout; validate status, JSON shape, matching id, and result XOR error; validate 0x quantity syntax and convert with BigInt. Test an RPC error under HTTP 200, malformed response, timeout, and a value above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Implement and adversarially test a four-leaf Keccak Merkle tree.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Specify leaf encoding, pair ordering, and odd-node policy; build levels, return sibling+side proofs, recompute root in verify, and reject mutated leaf/order/proof. Assert Ethereum Keccak differs from SHA3-256 and avoid ambiguous packed concatenation.

proposedPrompts.topicTitle: The EVM as a state machine
proposedPrompts.promptText: Implement the minimum interpreter needed to demonstrate deterministic execution and REVERT rollback.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Track pc, stack, byte-addressed memory, journaled storage, remaining gas, and halt status for PUSH1/ADD/MLOAD/MSTORE/SLOAD/SSTORE/STOP/REVERT. Wrap arithmetic modulo 2^256; reject underflow/invalid opcode/out-of-gas; commit storage only on successful halt.
